fatal_errors: The proposed Ti/Ti–Ni coating plus spark-plasma sintering does not reconstruct the target intervention: liquid-metal dealloying of directionally segregated WTaVTi in molten Cu at 1200 °C for 96 h.
The starting material is misidentified as an already formed W–Cu composite rather than an as-cast WTaVTi precursor with W/Ta-rich dendrites and sacrificial Ti/V-rich interdendritic channels.

The proposed graded W–Ti–Cu reaction zone conflicts with the target structural mediator: bicontinuous RHEA and nearly pure Cu channels separated by a spontaneously formed approximately 300 nm W-rich interlayer.

The cited evidence concerns micrometer-scale Ti/Ni coatings on diamond in an HEA matrix and reports primarily mechanical and interfacial-bonding effects; it does not validate nanometer-scale Ti/Ti–Ni coatings on W, W–Cu thermal conductivity, irradiation stability, or the claimed SPS conditions.

Fusion-relevant irradiation is treated generically and as direct testing of the composite, whereas the target used 25 keV He+ screening of precursor dendrites as a proxy and explicitly did not establish irradiation performance of the finished composite.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses the broad engineering objective of reducing W–Cu interfacial defects and improving heat transport, and its coated-versus-uncoated experiment could test its own central claim. However, it misses essentially every target-specific element: precursor chemistry and morphology, selective liquid-metal dealloying, processing temperature and duration, bicontinuous architecture, W-rich passivation layer, thermal range and crossover above pure W, and the limited proxy nature of the helium-irradiation results. The proposed alternative is not adequately supported because both cited passages concern Ti/Ni-coated diamond/HEA composites with 10–20 micrometer coatings, not W–Cu interfaces or thermal and irradiation performance. The stated 20–50 nm coating, Ti-to-Ni optimization, 900–1000 °C SPS window, and service limit of 550 °C therefore lack relevant evidence. The falsification design is comparatively strong, although it should specify a single irradiation species, energy, fluence, quantitative acceptance thresholds, and pre-irradiation conductivity controls.
